description: Common aerospace materials S-N curve parameters for acoustic fatigue analysis
reference: MIL-HDBK-5J / MMPDS-17 / SAE Fatigue Design Handbook
note: All stress values in MPa. Kt = 1.0 corresponds to unnotched (smooth) specimen baseline.

materials.description: Common aircraft fuselage skin and lower wing skin aluminum alloy. Good fatigue resistance with moderate strength.
High-strength aluminum alloy used in upper wing skins, bulkheads, and fuselage frames. Higher strength than 2024-T3 but lower fracture toughness.
Aerospace titanium alloy with excellent strength-to-weight ratio. Used in engine mounts, nacelle structures, and high-temperature acoustic environments up to 400°C.
Medium-carbon low-alloy steel. Used in landing gear components and high-strength structural fittings. Good hardenability and fatigue resistance.
Ultra-high-strength silicon-modified 4340 steel. Used in landing gear, flap tracks, and critical structural members. Superior strength and toughness.
Nickel-based superalloy for high-temperature acoustic environments (up to 650°C). Used in engine exhaust structures, afterburner liners, and hot-section acoustic panels.
Precipitation-hardening martensitic stainless steel. Used in actuator components, fasteners, and moderately elevated temperature applications. Good corrosion resistance.
